# Arithmetic projection coefficients and certified centroid recovery

This is an explicit coefficient-based regime criterion in arbitrary n,d.
It does not prove the target for bodies whose coefficient error is large.
The center is rounded only after a uniform all-halfspace error is proved;
positive depth then proves its membership in the actual mixed set.

Fix n>=1,d>=0, D=n+d, and a unimodular basis for the integer coordinates.
All notation below is in those coordinates. Such a change leaves mixed
measure unchanged and has absolute ambient determinant one. For a compact
convex set K and I subset {1,...,n}, let pi_I delete exactly the integer
coordinates in I, and set

    A_I(K)=mu_(n-|I|,d)(pi_I K),
    A_empty(K)=mu_(n,d)(K).

The projections retain all actual fibers, including lower-dimensional
ones; their d-volume may be zero. The last quotient, when all integer
coordinates are removed, uses ordinary d-volume (counting a nonempty
singleton if d=0). These A_I are exactly the coefficients of the
unimodular zonotope polynomial proved in
`candidate 372cc3158e8582ae`.

## 1. A finite coefficient discrepancy for every actual cap

For every compact convex K, including an empty or lower-dimensional one,

    |mu_(n,d)(K)-vol_D(K)|
       <=sum_(I nonempty) A_I(K).                              (1)

For n=1, use Fubini along the integer coordinate. A nonempty real interval
has integer-point count and length differing in absolute value by at
most one, including a singleton or an interval with no integer sample.
Integrating this error over its projection proves (1). The statement is
also true when the continuous dimension is zero.

Induct on n. First replace summation over coordinate 1 by integration,
keeping the other integer coordinates sampled. This changes the total
by at most A_{1}(K), by the same interval argument. Call the resulting
partially continuous measure B. The induction hypothesis applied to its
remaining n-1 integer coordinates bounds |B-vol_D(K)| by

    sum_(nonempty J subset {2,...,n}) B_J,

where B_J is the mixed measure of pi_J K with coordinate 1 continuous.
For each J, the one-coordinate estimate again gives

    B_J<=A_J(K)+A_(J union {1})(K).

The error A_{1} together with these two terms for every nonempty J is
exactly the sum in (1). This proves the induction. Every use of Fubini
concerns the actual convex line sections of the given set; no sum is
replaced by an integral without its displayed error.

Applying (1) to K=C intersect H and using projection monotonicity gives
the uniform bound

    mu(C intersect H)>=vol_D(C intersect H)-E,
    E=sum_(I nonempty) A_I(C),                                 (2)

for every CLOSED ambient halfspace H. Equation (1) also gives
vol_D(C)>=mu(C)-E. A halfspace boundary may contain entire positive-mass
integer fibers; the interval-count estimate includes those boundary
values exactly.

## 2. Uniform continuous cap cost of an integer displacement

Let C be a full D-dimensional convex body with ordinary volume V>0,
ordinary centroid c, and let

    y=c+(delta_1,...,delta_n,0,...,0).

No membership of y in C is assumed here. Let V_i=vol_(D-1)(pi_i C), where
this projection is now measured in its FULL continuous ambient dimension.
For every closed halfspace H through y,

    vol_D(C intersect H)>=Gamma_D V-sum_i |delta_i| V_i.         (3)

Here Gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D. Start with the parallel cap through c, whose
volume is at least Gamma_D V by ordinary Grünbaum. Move its boundary
successively through the coordinate displacements delta_i. If the i-th
integer normal coefficient is zero, that displacement changes nothing.
Otherwise, on each real line parallel to e_i its scalar cutoff changes
by exactly delta_i. The cap's captured interval length changes by at
most |delta_i|. Fubini bounds the total possible loss by |delta_i| V_i.
Summing the finite losses proves (3), for all coupled normal directions.

Apply the upper side of (1) to pi_i C, with its remaining n-1 integer
coordinates, to obtain

    V_i<=sum_(I containing i) A_I(C).                           (4)

The n=1 case of (4) is equality: no integer coordinate remains in pi_i C.

## 3. One deterministic rounded point, with membership proved afterward

Round each integer coordinate of c to a nearest integer, fixing either
choice deterministically at a tie, and leave its continuous coordinates
unchanged. Denote the resulting point by y, and its displacements by
delta_i, so |delta_i|<=1/2. Combining (2)-(4) proves the following raw
bound for EVERY closed containing halfspace of y:

    mu(C intersect H)>=B_delta,

    B_delta=Gamma_D M
       -sum_(I nonempty)
          [Gamma_D+1+sum_(i in I)|delta_i|] A_I(C),
    M=mu(C).                                                   (5)

Indeed a containing cap can first be shifted through y, which only
decreases its mass, and (3) applies there. If V and the V_i are known,
the sharper direct lower bound Gamma_D V-E-sum_i |delta_i|V_i can be
used before replacing V by M-E and applying (4).

Crucially, if B_delta>0, then y ACTUALLY BELONGS to S=C intersect
(Z^n times R^d). Its integer coordinates are already integral. If it
were outside the compact convex C, strict separation would give a
closed containing halfspace with empty intersection with C, contradicting
(5). Thus positivity proves the missing membership; it was never
presumed during the cap comparison. The same argument rules out lying
outside conv(S), if that additional fact is desired.

The simpler, rounding-independent quantity

    B=Gamma_D M
       -sum_(I nonempty) [Gamma_D+1+|I|/2] A_I(C)                (6)

satisfies B_delta>=B. These are exact finite inequalities, not statements
that an arbitrary centroid rounding is safe.

## 4. Explicit OC criterion and the heavy-fiber alternative

Assume M>0, so the full mixed-volume case is nonvacuous, and let
Gamma_0=1. If

    sum_(I nonempty) [Gamma_D+1+|I|/2] A_I(C)
       <=[Gamma_D-2^(-n)Gamma_d] M,                            (7)

then B>=2^(-n)Gamma_d M>0. The deterministic rounded point from Section 3
is in S and satisfies the exact OC target for every closed ambient
halfspace. No lattice-width, inradius, fiber-shape, or fixed-dimension
assumption enters (7); the condition is an explicit inequality in the
actual arithmetic coefficients. It is NOT asserted to hold for all C.

Independently, an ordinary centroid in a largest positive d-volume fiber
has raw depth at least Gamma_d W, where W=max_z vol_d(C_z); for d=0,
W=1 and the point itself supplies that counting mass. Consequently the
unconditional, possibly weak, combined bound is

    max_(y in S) depth_S(y)
       >=max{Gamma_d W/M, max(0,B)/M}.                         (8)

When B>0 its term has the certified rounded center. When B<=0 that term
asserts only the trivial nonnegative bound, so no out-of-body point is
selected. The first term handles an actual heavy fiber; the second
handles small projected-coefficient error. Intermediate cases not covered
by either sharp threshold remain unresolved.

These claims concern q=d and M>0. A lower intrinsic-dimensional mixed
intersection is not treated by replacing its measure with the zero
ambient-fiber d-volume in this note. The full OC goal is not resolved
by the conditional criterion (7).
